rv.q: The result is a brilliant exhibition of how theatre can create magic.
The Royal Shakespeare Company's stellar stage show has all the thrillingly staged battles, gory deaths and, yes, dragons that the most bloodthirsty fan could hope for.
This prequel to the TV series has one joust after another, spectacular stagecraft and plenty of modern resonance.
It’s a triumph; a soaring, surging spectacle and a latter-day history play, both serious and popular.
Inevitably, the first 40 minutes or so is largely concerned with exposition and introductions of Houses, characters and organisations.
The Mad King is a triumphant tragedy that perfectly captures the spirit of George R.R. Martin’s work and transposes it to a new medium.
The Game of Thrones franchise has yet another worthwhile and lucrative spin-off on its hands.

cn.t: Critics hail this RSC prequel as a gripping, spectacular triumph that channels Shakespeare's history plays with dragons. Despite a near-four-hour runtime and occasional density, the production satisfies fans with soaring stagecraft and deeper thematic exploration.
